articles.headline: Reba Hore enters centennial year with wider artistic recognition
articles.summary: Artist Reba Hore's vision is receiving wider recognition as she enters her centennial year. Her work, rooted in everyday life and shaped by politics, love, and solitude, reveals a deep humanity and a lifelong commitment to her craft. Major exhibitions are being held in Kolkata and Bengaluru to mark the occasion.

articles.headline: Lokesh Kanagaraj and Wamiqa Gabbi star in Tamil Devdas adaptation
articles.summary: Director Arun Matheswaran has adapted Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay’s novel Devdas into a Tamil film. The production stars Lokesh Kanagaraj, best known for directing Kaithi and Vikram, alongside Wamiqa Gabbi and Sanjana for a theatrical release.

articles.headline: Ryan Murphy creates thriller series The Shards for JioHotstar
articles.summary: Created by Ryan Murphy and Bret Easton Ellis, The Shards is a thriller series set in 1981 Los Angeles. Based on Ellis's novel, it follows a 17-year-old student whose life is unsettled by the arrival of a mysterious new student.

articles.headline: Japanese musical Linda Linda Linda begins streaming on MUBI
articles.summary: MUBI is streaming the 2015 Japanese musical film Linda Linda Linda. The story follows an all-girl rock band that recruits a new member after their lead singer quits on the eve of a major competition. It stars Bae Doona and Aki Maeda.

articles.headline: Netflix series Operation Safed Sagar dramatizes the Kargil War
articles.summary: Operation Safed Sagar is a six-episode Netflix limited series focused on the Indian Air Force's Golden Arrows squadron during the Kargil War. Created by Kushal Srivastava, the drama features an ensemble cast including Jimmy Shergill and Dia Mirza.

articles.headline: Hampi Art Labs hosts Red Rocks, Rivers and Monkeys exhibition
articles.summary: Hampi Art Labs is presenting an exhibition of photographs and video installations titled Red Rocks, Rivers and Monkeys. Curated by Yasufumi Nakamori, the show features works by Atul Bhalla and Robert Zhao Renhui inspired by the ecology of the Tungabhadra Basin.

articles.headline: Sameksha gallery celebrates anniversary with contemporary art exhibition
articles.summary: Sameksha gallery's first-anniversary exhibition, Close | Far—Lean In, Step Back, features works by Kavita Nayyar, Savya Jain, and Aman Kumar Bavaria. The show explores how scale shapes perception and intimacy in contemporary art.

articles.headline: Gen Z entrepreneurs turn to hacker houses for business growth
articles.summary: Indian Gen Z entrepreneurs are increasingly using hacker houses and startup residencies to build products and find mentorship. These shared living and working spaces in hubs like Bengaluru provide resources, investor access, and funding opportunities for early-stage founders.

articles.headline: Vineet Nayar emphasizes the need for corporate AI ethics codes
articles.summary: In his new book, Humans First, Machines Second, veteran leader Vineet Nayar argues that companies must adopt AI codes of ethics to address internal biases. He warns that failing to guide employees on data usage and legality can weaken trust with customers and staff.

articles.headline: Understanding muscle memory is crucial for beginner fitness journeys
articles.summary: Fitness expert Pulasta Dhar explains that muscle memory is a cognitive phase essential for learning new movement patterns. Consistency in exercise helps the body understand how to move and manage weights effectively as a beginner.

articles.headline: Hand-held fans become essential accessories amidst rising Indian heat
articles.summary: As summer temperatures and humidity rise across India, portable hand-held fans from brands like Nuuk and JisuLife have become necessary gadgets. Modern designs offer improved cooling and USB charging, making them popular fashion accessories.

articles.headline: Salinger's Catcher in the Rye remains relevant after 75 years
articles.summary: J.D. Salinger's classic novel The Catcher in the Rye continues to resonate with readers 75 years after its publication. The story of Holden Caulfield's disillusionment, grief, and search for authenticity offers emotional honesty that remains relevant in the digital age.

articles.headline: Census 2027 must accurately categorize India's growing single population
articles.summary: Census 2027 needs to distinguish between cohabiting and married individuals to accurately reflect social changes. India had 71 million single women in 2011, and proper enumeration is vital for securing welfare benefits and legal rights for the single population.

articles.headline: Netflix romcom Voicemails for Isabelle explores grief and connection
articles.summary: The Netflix film Voicemails for Isabelle stars Zoey Deutch as a woman coping with her sister's death by leaving voicemails on an old number. The story features a romantic twist and has been praised for its soundtrack and comedic timing.

articles.headline: Owais Yaqoob celebrates MMA victory with Kashmiri cultural symbols
articles.summary: Indian MMA fighter Owais Yaqoob defeated world champion Delyan Georgiev in Bulgaria while showcasing his Kashmiri identity. He appeared in the ring wearing a traditional Tilla-embroidered shawl and a Karakul cap alongside the national flag.

articles.headline: Historian Manu S. Pillai reflects on the repurposing of monuments
articles.summary: Historian Manu S. Pillai examines how iconic political buildings, such as the Hyderabad residency and various Mughal structures, are eventually repurposed for mundane uses. He notes that the intended dignity of historical monuments often yields to the practical needs of later generations.

articles.headline: Paramita Sen chronicles the history of Batanagar in new book
articles.summary: Paramita Sen’s book, Batanagar: A Personal History of India’s Forgotten Company Town, explores the industrial township built by the Bata company near Kolkata. The work examines the model of corporate paternalism and its eventual decline in the late 20th century.

articles.headline: San Francisco’s Japantown remains a vibrant hub of Japanese culture
articles.summary: San Francisco’s Japantown, the oldest of three remaining in the U.S., hosts historic establishments like Hinodeya and Soko Hardware. The enclave preserves Japanese culinary and cultural traditions through specialized dining and artisanal shops.

articles.headline: Indian boxers secure seven gold medals at 2026 Commonwealth Games
articles.summary: India finished fourth at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, led by a record-breaking performance from its boxers. The squad won seven gold and three silver medals, with standout victories from Arundhati Choudhary, Preeti Pawar, and Sachin Siwach.

articles.headline: Indian Super League seeks turnaround with upcoming media rights tender
articles.summary: The Indian Super League is looking for a new broadcast partner for a four-year cycle starting 2026-27. Following Jamshedpur FC's withdrawal due to financial unviability, clubs are hoping for a high-value deal to sustain operations and central revenue pools.

articles.headline: Recent films and books explore reconciliation through journeys to Pakistan
articles.summary: New creative works, including the films Ikkis and Main Vaapas Aaunga, are moving away from caricatures to explore humanistic Indo-Pak narratives. These stories emphasize shared history, family reconnections, and personal growth facilitated by crossing borders.

articles.headline: NBFC stocks slide following RBI proposal to bar revolving credit
articles.summary: Shares of major NBFCs like Bajaj Finance and Tata Capital fell after an RBI proposal suggested that non-banks should only offer term loans. If implemented, this would prohibit revolving credit facilities unless the NBFC holds a credit card license, impacting growth and yields.

articles.headline: Indian government considers subsidies to promote electric induction cookstoves
articles.summary: The Indian government is planning subsidies and lower duties to boost induction cookstove adoption, aiming to reduce reliance on imported LPG. The plan includes upgrading distribution infrastructure to manage higher electricity loads for residential consumers.

articles.headline: FMCG CEO salaries rise despite sluggish demand and weak volumes
articles.summary: Top consumer goods companies like Marico and Tata Consumer raised CEO pay in FY26 to secure talent amidst macroeconomic uncertainty. Marico CEO Saugata Gupta earned the highest total pay at ₹47.24 crore, a 20.7% increase from the previous year.

articles.headline: Shorter Independence Day weekend shifts travel demand to drive-to getaways
articles.summary: With Independence Day falling on a Saturday, Indian travellers are opting for drive-to destinations like Lonavala and Coorg over traditional leisure spots. Hotel chains report a 16-20% increase in city property bookings due to the compressed holiday window.

articles.headline: Himachal apple production projected to dip by one-third in 2026
articles.summary: Indian apple prices may remain high as production in Himachal Pradesh is projected to drop to 493,465 tonnes in 2026 from 699,876 tonnes in 2025. The decline is attributed to horticultural trends and data reviewed from the state department.

articles.headline: Centre increases nationwide surveillance and preparedness for leptospirosis
articles.summary: The Indian government has stepped up its plan to contain leptospirosis, a bacterial disease transmitted via contaminated water or soil. The move focuses on heightened surveillance during the monsoon season to protect both humans and livestock.

articles.headline: Electric vehicle retail sales in India reach record monthly high
articles.summary: EV retail sales reached a record 327,901 units in July, a 66% year-on-year increase. One in eight vehicles retailed in India is now electric, with the previous record set only in June, according to the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations.

articles.headline: IMD warns of extremely heavy rainfall in eastern and northern India
articles.summary: The India Meteorological Department warned of heavy to extremely heavy rainfall across eastern, northwestern, and southern India over the next three days. Low-pressure systems have created flash flood risks for Odisha, West Bengal, and Jharkhand.

articles.headline: Hindalco reports 75% profit jump but maintains caution on bidding
articles.summary: Hindalco Industries Ltd reported a ₹7,013 crore net profit for the June quarter, beating estimates. Despite strong earnings and a 32% revenue increase, the company stated it will remain financially disciplined in bidding for bauxite mines amidst rising competition.

articles.headline: Nifty Smallcap 250 climbs 2.4% as Indian benchmarks gain ground
articles.summary: Indian equities ended the week higher, with the Nifty Smallcap 250 outperforming the broader market with a 2.4% gain. Metal, capital goods, and auto stocks led the weekly rise, although indices faced a slight decline on Friday.

articles.headline: India Resurgence Fund acquires majority stake in Fine Edge Engineering
articles.summary: IndiaRF, a JV between Piramal and Bain Capital, acquired a majority stake in Fine Edge Engineering from Ashok Iron Works. The deal, valued at up to ₹2,200 crore, focuses on iron casting and machining for heavy engine applications and global supply chains.

articles.headline: Hero MotoCorp to launch electric motorcycles starting from 2027
articles.summary: Hero MotoCorp plans to enter the electric motorcycle segment in 2027, timing the launch ahead of Delhi's proposed 2028 ban on ICE two-wheelers. The company is developing dedicated platforms for both commuter and performance electric motorcycles.

articles.headline: CMS Info Systems targets 20% revenue from technology and payments
articles.summary: CMS Info Systems plans to double the revenue contribution of its technology and payments vertical to 20% by FY30. The company is expanding its AI surveillance and remote monitoring solutions across 15 industries, moving beyond its traditional cash management core.

articles.headline: Sustainability experts urge companies to embed net zero into business strategy
articles.summary: At the Mint Sustainability Summit 2026, experts highlighted that the next phase of decarbonization requires circularity and long-term partnerships. Leaders from Saint-Gobain and BMW noted that sustainability is now a strategic business priority rather than just a compliance issue.

articles.headline: Deloitte introduces framework to measure strategic returns from sustainability
articles.summary: Deloitte South Asia unveiled a new framework to help companies evaluate sustainability as a driver of enterprise value. The approach shifts the focus from simple regulatory compliance to long-term financial and strategic gains like improved access to global markets.

articles.headline: Shapoorji Pallonji Group offers $2.7 billion bond issue to wealthy investors
articles.summary: The SP Group is offering its record ₹21,350 crore bond issue to high-net-worth individuals and family offices through private wealth platforms. The debt, backed by a stake in Tata Sons, offers exposure to the holding company's potential future IPO value.

articles.headline: Vedanta’s subsidiary Balco wins auction for Karlapat bauxite block in Odisha
articles.summary: Bharat Aluminium Co. Ltd (Balco) emerged as the preferred bidder for the Karlapat bauxite block with a record 175% premium. The win secures mineral reserves of 248 million tonnes, supporting Vedanta's strategic backward integration and capacity expansion plans.

articles.headline: Global PE funds evaluate investment in Pricol’s demerged DICVS business
articles.summary: Advent International and EQT are among private equity players interested in investing in Pricol’s newly demerged smart mobility and connectivity unit. The deal could value the driver information and connected vehicle solutions business at approximately ₹5,000 crore.

articles.headline: India's crude oil import bill rises 26 percent despite volume fall
articles.summary: India's crude import bill for Q1 2026-27 rose 26% year-on-year to $49 billion, even as volumes fell 18% to 59.7 million tonnes. The discrepancy is driven by global oil prices rising to $82 per barrel from $73 last year, fueled by West Asia conflicts. Russia remains the top supplier, accounting for 40% of imports, followed by Iraq and Saudi Arabia. The weak rupee also impacted the total cost.

articles.headline: Iran seeks to bar US and Israeli ships from Strait Hormuz
articles.summary: Iran is seeking to prohibit US and Israeli vessels from traversing the Strait of Hormuz, demanding compensation for 'hostile' actions. The proposal, discussed in an Iran-Oman deal, aims to regulate passage through the critical global energy chokepoint. While Iran claims the move is for regional security, the US State Department dismissed the effort as contrary to international maritime law.

articles.headline: Downloading Maoist literature is not a criminal offence, rules Mumbai court
articles.summary: A Mumbai sessions court granted pre-arrest bail to seven TISS students, ruling that merely downloading or reading Maoist literature does not constitute a criminal offence. The court noted that unless the material is used to incite violence or aid banned organizations, possession alone is legal. However, the court denied relief to two other students over alleged active links to Maoist groups.

articles.headline: Global solar capacity triples to 3TW as India leads market expansion
articles.summary: Global solar energy capacity has reached 3 terawatts, with India emerging as one of the fastest-growing markets. India currently has 141GW of installed solar capacity, representing 27% of its total power capacity. While solar growth has outpaced coal and gas for a decade, experts highlight remaining challenges in storage, grid reliability, and the intermittent nature of solar generation.

articles.headline: Nearly fifty percent of Bengaluru voters face deletion in election survey
articles.summary: An intensive revision of electoral rolls in Bengaluru has flagged nearly 50% of the city's voters for potential deletion. The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) identified 1.1 crore electors under 'ASD' categories (absent, shifted, dead, or duplicate). Bengaluru South saw the highest proportion of anomalies at 50.7%. Citizens' groups have raised concerns over the accuracy of door-to-door surveys.

articles.headline: CBI cracks NEET paper leak case using WhatsApp and app trails
articles.summary: The CBI has solved the NEET-UG paper leak case by tracing digital trails on WhatsApp and a dedicated mobile app used by the perpetrators. Investigations revealed that solved question papers were distributed to select candidates in Jharkhand and Bihar via these platforms. Several masterminds, including professional tutors and administrative staff, have been arrested as the probe continues.

articles.headline: Telangana high court slams government over unsustainable freebie schemes
articles.summary: The Telangana High Court has criticized the state government for its proliferation of freebie schemes, warning that 'even Kuber would give up' if the trend continues. The court was hearing a plea regarding the non-payment of dues to the Cantonment Board, noting that resources are being diverted to vote-catching populist measures while essential administrative and civic debts remain unpaid.

articles.headline: Air India pilots receive salary hikes of up to 15 percent
articles.summary: Air India has announced salary hikes for its pilots ranging from 8% to 15%, the largest increase since its acquisition by the Tata Group. Senior commanders can now earn up to Rs 8.3 lakh per month, while first officers will receive around Rs 3.3 lakh. The move aims to retain talent and boost morale as the airline expands its fleet and international route network.

articles.headline: Government looks to revamp investment treaties after years of discussion
articles.summary: The Indian government is set to revise its Model Bilateral Investment Treaty (BIT) to address roadblocks in attracting foreign direct investment. Proposed changes include easier dispute settlement mechanisms and clearer protections for international investors. The revamp aims to remove 'red flags' that have previously deterred large-scale foreign investment in the manufacturing and tech sectors.

articles.headline: AI creates 83,000 jobs in India as tech hiring outpaces automation
articles.summary: A Nomura Economics report finds that artificial intelligence has created 83,100 jobs in India recently, contradicting fears of mass displacement. While AI has automated some junior entry-level tasks, it has spurred a massive demand for skilled developers, data scientists, and AI-integration experts. India now accounts for nearly 15% of global AI-related talent hiring.

articles.headline: Thailand school shooting leaves seven dead as 14-year-old student opens fire
articles.summary: A 14-year-old boy killed seven people, including teachers and fellow students, at a school in Thailand's Bang Kruai. The shooter, who reportedly suffered from extreme academic stress, used a handgun taken from his home. Police captured the teen after a brief standoff. The incident has triggered a national debate in Thailand over gun control and the mental health crisis among students.

articles.headline: Supreme Court closes 40-year-old Bofors corruption case appeal
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India has dismissed an appeal seeking to reopen the Bofors corruption case, officially ending the four-decade-old legal saga. The court ruled that the delay in filing the appeal was inexcusable and that there was no merit in the fresh evidence presented. The case, involving alleged kickbacks in a 1986 artillery gun deal, had long impacted Indian political discourse.

articles.headline: Bengaluru startup unveils first indigenous 800kN liquid fuel rocket engine
articles.summary: Space startup Bellatrix Aerospace has unveiled India's first privately developed 800kN full-flow staged combustion rocket engine. Named 'Everest,' the engine uses liquid oxygen and methane as propellants. It is designed for high-lift launch vehicles and marks a significant milestone in India's private space sector, offering reusable technology for commercial satellite launches.

articles.headline: US Senate clears bill for tariffs over Russian oil
articles.summary: The US Senate passed a bill allowing the Commerce Department to impose tariffs on Russian oil, gas, and coal imports, reversing a previous decision and potentially affecting global energy markets.

articles.headline: Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi Arabia finalize mutual defense cooperation deal
articles.summary: Pakistan, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia finalized a mutual defense cooperation deal during talks on the sidelines of the three-country meeting on countering Islamophobia. The agreement aims to enhance military collaboration and strategic alignment.

articles.headline: Delhi cabinet approves 25% local quota in PV varsities bill
articles.summary: The Delhi cabinet approved a bill reserving 25% of seats for Delhi-residing students in private universities, aiming to provide more opportunities for local students in higher education.

articles.headline: US regulator orders airlines to fix engine cracks by May
articles.summary: The US Federal Aviation Administration ordered airlines to inspect and repair engine cracks on Boeing 737 aircraft by May, affecting 177 planes and addressing potential safety issues.

articles.headline: Vivek Vihar fire report reveals illegal flats and safety lapses
articles.summary: A fire audit report for a Delhi-based hospital found illegal construction and multiple safety lapses, including violations of fire safety norms, after a deadly fire incident. The hospital owner was previously arrested.

articles.headline: Politician cannot approach SC directly with 'Mahtab' petition
articles.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that a politician cannot directly file a petition under Article 32 using the name of a private individual, to bypass legal scrutiny for political gains.

articles.headline: August monsoon shows improved rainfall after deficient June
articles.summary: After a deficient June, monsoon rainfall improved significantly in August, with 25.1 mm in the first week, reducing the deficit. Some regions still face deficits, while others recorded surpluses, showing varied geographical distribution.

articles.headline: MEA rebuffs US lawmakers on FCRA bill criticism
articles.summary: India's External Affairs Ministry rejected concerns raised by US lawmakers regarding the proposed FCRA amendments, stating they are a matter of India's internal policy aimed at regulating foreign funding of NGOs.

articles.headline: 3 NEET paper leak suspects linked to public servants
articles.summary: CBI sources indicate three suspects involved in the NEET paper leak case are connected to public servants, including former and current officers, highlighting potential systemic corruption.

articles.headline: NCR sinks under neglect as heavy rains cause waterlogging
articles.summary: Heavy rainfall caused severe waterlogging and traffic jams across Delhi-NCR, exposing inadequate urban infrastructure and drainage systems, leading to disruptions and public inconvenience.

articles.headline: CBI to question officials on Kalvery issue projects (2012-2022)
articles.summary: CBI plans to question officials involved in projects on the Cauvery river basin between 2012-2022, as part of an ongoing investigation, following a Supreme Court directive on water sharing disputes.

articles.headline: Government fast-tracks approval for 9,310 Km highway projects
articles.summary: The government aims to fast-track approval for 9,310 km of national highway projects to boost infrastructure development and connectivity across the country, prioritizing completion within specified timelines.

articles.headline: Vajpayee's government only one to return Kashmir pandits
articles.summary: The article discusses former PM Vajpayee's efforts to resettle Kashmiri Pandits in the Valley, noting his government was the only one that initiated substantial steps for their return.

articles.headline: 'Quit India' movement begins, British crack down with arrests
articles.summary: Excerpts from reports on the start of the Quit India movement detail widespread arrests and firings by British authorities against nationalists, highlighting the intense resistance and suppressive measures.

articles.headline: NEET paper leak network spanned Okhla to Pune
articles.summary: An extensive network for the NEET paper leak involved individuals from Okhla to Pune, highlighting alleged roles of coaching centers, distributors, and middlemen in disseminating question papers for financial gain.

articles.headline: EC extends SIR deadline, BLOs get nine more days
articles.summary: The Election Commission extended the deadline for the Special Summary Revision (SIR) and granted Block Level Officers (BLOs) nine additional days to verify voter data.

articles.headline: Shivakumar advocates for Karnataka caste survey
articles.summary: Karnataka Deputy CM D.K. Shivakumar called for the immediate release and implementation of the state's caste survey report, emphasizing its importance for social justice and equitable distribution of resources.

articles.headline: Magellan's 250th taste expedition across Bengaluru's "Thindi" street food
articles.summary: A culinary journey through Bengaluru's famous "Thindi" street food scene, celebrating its diverse flavors and unique eating experience, likened to an expedition.

articles.headline: Priyank Kharge criticizes PM Modi's absence from Parliament
articles.summary: Karnataka minister Priyank Kharge criticized PM Modi's absence from Parliament during crucial debates, questioning his commitment to democratic processes and accountability.

articles.headline: BBMP clears 10,000 tonnes waste in two months
articles.summary: The Bengaluru civic body (BBMP) cleared over 10,000 metric tonnes of waste from the city's storm drains and public areas within two months, aiming to improve sanitation and prevent waterlogging.

articles.headline: Health department forms 30 teams to check for fever
articles.summary: The health department deployed 30 teams to conduct door-to-door fever surveys and detect infectious diseases early, especially in areas with high incidence, to prevent outbreaks.

articles.headline: Upa Lokayukta acts on Hampi dormitory violations
articles.summary: The Karnataka Upa Lokayukta initiated suo motu action against 54 officials regarding alleged violations and irregularities in the construction and maintenance of dormitories in Hampi.

articles.headline: BJP to question Congress in upcoming house session
articles.summary: The BJP plans to aggressively question the Congress government during the upcoming legislative session on various issues, including its governance and alleged policy failures.

articles.headline: HC quashes cruelty case against mother-in-law
articles.summary: The High Court quashed a criminal complaint of cruelty filed by a woman against her mother-in-law, citing lack of sufficient evidence and potential misuse of legal provisions.

articles.headline: Horatti quits after no confidence motion threat
articles.summary: Basavaraj Horatti, a senior MLC, resigned from his position after the government threatened to bring a no-confidence motion against him, averting a political confrontation.

articles.headline: Won't yield on Cauvery rights, open to talks: Vijay
articles.summary: Karnataka CM Vijayendra stated the state will not compromise on its Cauvery river water rights and the Mekedatu project, but remains open to discussions with Tamil Nadu to find a solution.

articles.headline: TN CM withdraws plea regarding Hatha festival
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu CM M.K. Stalin withdrew a petition challenging the central government's directive to celebrate the Hatha yoga festival, after the Centre clarified it wasn't mandatory.

articles.headline: Kerala HC extends hysterectomy leave to contractual employees
articles.summary: The Kerala High Court ruled that contractual women employees are entitled to 60 days of special leave for hysterectomy, aligning their benefits with permanent staff.

articles.headline: Polavaram PP-1 on track for 2027 completion
articles.summary: The Centre informed the Lok Sabha that the Polavaram Project Phase-1 is expected to be completed by 2027, with 70% of the project work finished and significant funds disbursed.

articles.headline: Speaker rejects CM Vijay's apology, refers DMK MLA to panel
articles.summary: The Speaker rejected CM Vijayendra's apology regarding remarks against the House and decided to refer the DMK MLA responsible for the remarks to the House privileges committee.

articles.headline: AP student arrested for murdering girlfriend
articles.summary: An engineering student was arrested in Andhra Pradesh for allegedly murdering his girlfriend, who was also a student, after an argument. Police investigations are ongoing.

articles.headline: Two cars run over medico in negligence case
articles.summary: A medical student was run over by two cars, leading to a "negligence" case against the drivers, highlighting road safety concerns.

articles.headline: NIA arrests 3 in Kerala illegal explosives case
articles.summary: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) arrested three individuals in Kerala for their alleged involvement in an illegal explosives manufacturing case, seizing incriminating materials.

articles.headline: YSRCP slams AP's move to scrap Disha Bill
articles.summary: The YSRCP criticized the Andhra Pradesh government's decision to scrap the Disha Bill, arguing it jeopardizes women's safety and weakens legal protections against crimes.

articles.headline: Former TDB chief among 3 booked in Sabarimala ghee case
articles.summary: The Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau booked a former Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB) chief and two others in a case related to alleged irregularities in the supply of ghee for Sabarimala temple.

articles.headline: Latha Rajinikanth unveils 'Makkal Medal' for social welfare
articles.summary: Latha Rajinikanth launched the 'Makkal Medal' initiative to recognize and reward individuals engaged in social welfare activities, encouraging citizen participation in community development.

articles.headline: CM Vijay calls MPs' meet on delimitation
articles.summary: Karnataka CM Vijayendra convened a meeting with MPs to discuss the impact of delimitation on the state's political representation and development projects, seeking a unified stance.

articles.headline: Amit Shah to visit Tamil Nadu on August 8-9
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah will visit Tamil Nadu on August 8-9, during which he will hold meetings with state BJP leaders and attend party events, strengthening political outreach.

articles.headline: No direction from RS Chair to Shah, Rijiju clarifies
articles.summary: Union Minister Kiren Rijiju clarified that the Rajya Sabha Chairman did not issue any direct directions to Amit Shah, refuting media reports of a specific instruction.

articles.headline: Opposition to press for Shah's statement on FCRA Bill
articles.summary: Opposition parties are likely to demand a statement from Amit Shah regarding the FCRA amendment bill, anticipating its tabling in Parliament and raising concerns about its implications.

articles.headline: PM, Badal meeting sparks BJP-Akali reunion buzz
articles.summary: A meeting between PM Modi and Sukhbir Badal fueled speculation of a potential reunion between BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) in Punjab politics.

articles.headline: GenZ's outreach to GenZ sparks slugfest
articles.summary: The article discusses a political slugfest emerging from GenZ-focused outreach campaigns, with various parties attempting to engage younger voters through social media and cultural trends.

articles.headline: SC to TMC MP: "Freedom fighters took bullets, you fear eggs?"
articles.summary: The Supreme Court questioned a TMC MP's plea for enhanced security, remarking on the triviality of fearing "eggs" compared to the sacrifices of freedom fighters.

articles.headline: Birbhum violence tapes manipulated, Manipur government tells SC
articles.summary: The Manipur government informed the Supreme Court that audio tapes related to the Birbhum violence case were manipulated, casting doubt on their authenticity in the ongoing investigation.

articles.headline: Modi government to balance responsibility
articles.summary: The Modi government is focused on balancing policy initiatives with electoral responsibilities, aiming for effective governance while preparing for upcoming elections.

articles.headline: Jharkhand students to probe cybercrime cases
articles.summary: Jharkhand government announced that only students from the state who have successfully completed specialized training will be allowed to investigate cybercrime cases.

articles.headline: Explore Porch: A cultural segment
articles.summary: A brief note on "Explore Porch," potentially a cultural segment or exhibition, inviting readers to engage with its content.

articles.headline: 3 of 6,500 Kashmiri Pandit families resettled in Valley
articles.summary: Only 3 out of 6,500 Kashmiri Pandit families, who sought to return to the Valley under a rehabilitation package, have been resettled, highlighting slow progress and ongoing challenges.

articles.headline: TN CM: No compromise on Cauvery, Mekedatu dam
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu CM asserted no compromise on the state's Cauvery water rights and demanded a halt to Karnataka's Mekedatu project, stating it violates existing agreements.

articles.headline: Vijay's wife withdraws petition to divorce him
articles.summary: Vijay's wife withdrew her petition seeking divorce from the actor, signaling a potential reconciliation or resolution of their marital dispute.

articles.headline: MP armed forces oppose community benefits
articles.summary: The Madhya Pradesh armed forces organization urged the government not to grant community-specific benefits, emphasizing that all personnel should be treated equally regardless of caste or religion.

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi: E20 to be major Lok Sabha poll plank
articles.summary: Rahul Gandhi indicated that the E20 biofuel blend program would be a significant electoral issue for the Congress in the upcoming Lok Sabha elections, focusing on farmers' benefits.

articles.headline: Security guard held for firing in air in Barimath
articles.summary: A security guard was arrested in Barimath for firing shots in the air during a celebration, leading to a police investigation into illegal use of firearms.

articles.headline: Man shot in gun display dies in ambulance crash
articles.summary: A man who was shot during a gun display died when the ambulance transporting him to the hospital crashed, adding to the tragic circumstances.

articles.headline: Army enhancing surveillance capabilities
articles.summary: The Indian Army is significantly upgrading its surveillance capabilities along the border regions to counter infiltration and monitor adversary movements more effectively.

articles.headline: Proposal to enhance counter-insurgency operations
articles.summary: A proposal is under consideration to enhance counter-insurgency operations in conflict zones, focusing on improved intelligence gathering and coordinated efforts with local forces.

articles.headline: SC: Harmonize RTI and data privacy laws
articles.summary: The Supreme Court emphasized the need to harmonize the Right to Information (RTI) Act with data privacy laws to balance transparency and individual privacy rights, amidst ongoing legal debates.

articles.headline: Centre mulls framework for 'offensive' OTT content
articles.summary: The government is considering a framework to regulate "offensive" content on Over-The-Top (OTT) platforms, aiming to balance artistic freedom with cultural sensitivities and public order.

articles.headline: India to get 2nd spaceport in Tamil Nadu
articles.summary: The Central government announced plans for India's second spaceport to be built in Tamil Nadu, enhancing the country's space launch capabilities and promoting regional development.

articles.headline: KVS exam results to be out in phases: CBSE
articles.summary: CBSE announced that Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan (KVS) exam results would be released in phases, with interviews for selected candidates beginning August 8th.

articles.headline: Amritsar Police Commissioner acquitted
articles.summary: The Amritsar Police Commissioner was acquitted in a case, after being accused of misconduct, following a court ruling that found insufficient evidence against him.

articles.headline: PVT bill seeks curbs on U-13 social media use
articles.summary: A private member's bill proposes restrictions on social media use for children under 13, aiming to protect young users from online harm and promote responsible digital habits.

articles.headline: Krishnadevaraya: 517 years since Vijayanagara empire
articles.summary: The article commemorates 517 years since Krishnadevaraya ascended the throne of the Vijayanagara Empire, highlighting his significant reign and architectural contributions, particularly the Hazara Rama temple.

articles.headline: Dakini refuses retirement: Poetry section
articles.summary: A cultural piece featuring poetry, exploring themes of spiritual awakening and the human condition, presented in a literary review format.

articles.headline: A Southern herstory: Review of "The Woman of No Consequence"
articles.summary: A review of "The Woman of No Consequence," a novel exploring the lives of women in Southern India through the lens of history, culture, and personal narratives.

articles.headline: A slave turns hero: Review of "The Rebel"
articles.summary: A review of "The Rebel," a novel about the struggles and triumphs of a slave who rises to become a hero, set against a backdrop of historical events.

articles.headline: Rebel, Rebel: A look at contemporary political theory
articles.summary: A review examining contemporary political theory and its reflections on current social and political developments, offering insights into modern governance and dissent.

articles.headline: A book that helps young adults
articles.summary: A brief highlight of a book recommended for young adults, focusing on themes relevant to their development and challenges.

articles.headline: Pablo Cartaya: "I cannot help being an optimist"
articles.summary: An interview with author Pablo Cartaya, who shares his optimistic outlook on life and writing, discussing his creative process and inspirations for his books targeting young readers.

articles.headline: Forktails, flycatchers, and pheasants: A birdwatching book review
articles.summary: A review of a book focused on various bird species, offering insights into birdwatching, avian behavior, and the natural world, appealing to nature enthusiasts.

articles.headline: Deep impact of social media and influencer culture
articles.summary: The article discusses the profound influence of social media and influencer culture on society, particularly among youth, exploring trends, psychological impacts, and the pursuit of online validation.

articles.headline: Just follow the crunch: Food review
articles.summary: A cultural piece exploring the popularity of fried chicken, specifically KFC, in India and its global presence, examining consumer preferences and market trends in fast food.

articles.headline: The 2026 name drop: Bollywood trends
articles.summary: A Bollywood-focused article discussing the increasing trend of celebrity children making their debuts, often with unique names, and the public's fascination with their entry into the industry.

articles.headline: Strike the mother lode: Friendships after marriage
articles.summary: A lifestyle piece exploring the dynamics of female friendships after marriage, emphasizing their importance for support and companionship, and how they evolve over time.

articles.headline: Gone with the trend: Online addictions
articles.summary: An article examining how online trends can become addictive, discussing 10 popular online obsessions that have faded, highlighting the transient nature of digital fads and their impact on users.

articles.headline: Turkey, Pakistan tighten defense alliance
articles.summary: Turkey and Pakistan deepened their defense cooperation with a new agreement, aiming to enhance military ties, joint exercises, and strategic collaboration in the region.

articles.headline: Teenager kills 7 in Thai shooting spree
articles.summary: A teenager opened fire in Thailand, killing 7 people, including his family members, and injuring several others in a shocking incident of gun violence.

articles.headline: US President's stance on 'birthing citizenship'
articles.summary: US President commented on 'birthing citizenship' despite a top court ruling, stating his intention to end it, sparking debate on immigration policy.

articles.headline: China confirms sanctions on US lawmakers
articles.summary: China confirmed sanctions against several US lawmakers in retaliation for their criticism regarding human rights issues in Xinjiang and Hong Kong.

articles.headline: US proposes $1.3B deal for chip plant
articles.summary: The US government proposed a $1.3 billion deal to a major chip manufacturer to build a semiconductor fabrication plant in the country, aiming to boost domestic chip production.

articles.headline: MEA orders removal of religious text from film
articles.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs issued an order for the removal of certain religious texts from a film, citing public nuisance and potential for communal disharmony.

articles.headline: RBI proposes curbs on NBFC revolving credit
articles.summary: RBI's proposal to impose stricter regulations on revolving credit offered by Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) has rattled markets, raising concerns about credit flow and profitability.

articles.headline: IndiGo in talks for regional jets
articles.summary: IndiGo is in discussions with major global aircraft manufacturers for acquiring regional jets, aiming to expand its network and boost connectivity to tier-2 and tier-3 cities.

articles.headline: India protects farmers' interests at BRICS
articles.summary: India highlighted its commitment to protecting farmers' interests at the BRICS agricultural ministers' meeting, advocating for fair trade policies and food security initiatives.

articles.headline: Relief for Dabur as HS, FSSAI pause claims
articles.summary: Dabur received relief as the Health Secretary and FSSAI paused claims against its products, following a review of alleged labeling violations, providing clarity to the company.

articles.headline: Oil companies confirm E20 petrol meets quality norms
articles.summary: Oil companies affirmed that E20 (20% ethanol blended petrol) meets all quality standards and specifications, assuring consumers of its performance and safety.

articles.headline: Hindalco Industries shares jump 7%
articles.summary: Shares of Hindalco Industries rose by 7% following positive market sentiment and strong performance reports, indicating investor confidence in the metal sector.

articles.headline: India frustrated by Sri Lanka Cricket XI on opening day
articles.summary: Indian cricket team faced frustration on the opening day against Sri Lanka Cricket XI, with cautious play and strong resistance from the hosts, leading to an even contest.

articles.headline: 'Everything looks smooth but that wasn't the case'
articles.summary: An interview with a prominent figure reflecting on challenges faced despite outward appearances of success, discussing the hidden struggles and complexities behind achievements.

articles.headline: SFI mulls reinventing training systems after quiet CWG
articles.summary: Following a subdued performance at the Commonwealth Games, the Swimming Federation of India (SFI) is considering significant reforms to its training systems to improve future results.

articles.headline: England striker Tony charged with assault
articles.summary: England striker was charged with assault following an incident, leading to legal proceedings and potential repercussions for his career.

articles.headline: Ashmita, Rakshita book semis showdown in Korea
articles.summary: Indian shuttlers Ashmita and Rakshita advanced to the semifinals in a badminton tournament in Korea, setting up an exciting showdown between the two.

articles.headline: Who after Satwik-Chirag in India's doubles pipeline?
articles.summary: The article explores the future of Indian badminton doubles after the success of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, identifying potential talent and strategies for developing new pairs.

articles.headline: Indian hockey captain: 'India has ability to upset anyone'
articles.summary: Indian men's hockey captain, Harmanpreet Singh, expressed confidence in the team's ability to surprise top opponents, highlighting their potential and strategic improvements ahead of upcoming tournaments.

articles.headline: IPL games called off in Myanmar
articles.summary: Indian Premier League (IPL) games scheduled to be held in Myanmar were called off due to logistical issues and prevailing political instability in the region.

articles.headline: Indian women win U-19 Asian C'ship final
articles.summary: The Indian women's U-19 cricket team clinched the Asian Championship title, defeating their opponents in the final match.

articles.headline: Travis Head wins Allan Border medal
articles.summary: Australian cricketer Travis Head was awarded the prestigious Allan Border Medal for his outstanding performance in the past year.

articles.headline: Tihagi bags silver in U-20 World Athletics
articles.summary: Indian athlete Tihagi won a silver medal at the U-20 World Athletics Championship, marking a significant achievement for the country.

articles.headline: CBI chargesheet exposes NEET paper leak network and modus operandi
articles.summary: The CBI filed a chargesheet against 13 individuals for the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak. The agency detailed a complex network moving papers from subject experts to students via middlemen. Modus operandi included using WhatsApp groups like 'World Cup 2026' and facilitators in Maharashtra. The probe continues as experts gain access to final sets of questions.

articles.headline: SBI posts highest-ever quarterly profit of ₹21,121 cr in Q1
articles.summary: State Bank of India (SBI) reported its highest-ever quarterly net profit of ₹21,121 crore for Q1, up 10% from the previous year. Net interest income rose 15% to ₹46,992 crore. Despite a decline in non-interest income and treasury income, the bank maintained strong performance driven by loan growth and lower loan-loss provisions. Gross NPA ratio improved to 2.47%.

articles.headline: India's supply-side strengthened amid repeated global shocks, says CEA
articles.summary: Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran stated India's ability to maintain high growth while reducing fiscal deficit reflects significant supply-side improvements. Speaking at the Fintech Festival, he highlighted resilience against shocks like Covid-19 and geopolitical tensions. He emphasized that future growth will depend on productivity and private sector investment.

articles.headline: Astrobane unveils Everest, India’s first FFSC engine for reusable rockets
articles.summary: Space-tech startup Astrobane launched Everest, India’s first 800 kN full-flow staged combustion (FFSC) engine. Built for reusable launch vehicles, the LOX-methane engine is designed for high efficiency and multiple restarts. The company plans its first flight by late 2028, aiming to compete globally with advanced propulsion technology for industrial-scale space activities.

articles.headline: Rice prices on the boil in domestic market on supply-demand gap
articles.summary: Prices of non-basmati rice varieties have increased by over 10% recently due to a supply-demand gap and fears of a deficient monsoon. Despite the government increasing the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for the 2026-27 crop year, retail prices for common varieties have risen by ₹5-10 per kg. Millers report tight supplies as paddy rates continue to climb.

articles.headline: Five States home to more than half of Jan Dhan beneficiaries
articles.summary: Five states—Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Madhya Pradesh, and Rajasthan—account for 54% of India's 58.7 crore Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) accounts. Uttar Pradesh leads with nearly 20% of the total. SBI holds the largest share of these accounts nationally at 30.9%, followed by Bank of Baroda. Financial inclusion efforts remain concentrated in these populated regions.

articles.headline: Godrej Consumer Products reports 19% Q1 revenue growth
articles.summary: Godrej Consumer Products Ltd (GCPL) saw consolidated revenue rise 19% to ₹4,225 crore for the quarter ended June 30. Net profit increased by 11% to ₹505 crore. Growth was led by the home care segment, up 12%, and personal care, up 11%. The company's international business in Africa, the US, and the Middle East performed strongly with 47% sales growth.

articles.headline: Hindalco Q1 profit rises 75% on strong metal prices
articles.summary: Aditya Birla Group’s Hindalco Industries reported a 75% surge in consolidated net profit to ₹7,013 crore for the June quarter. Revenue rose 32% to ₹84,825 crore, driven by robust metal prices and lower input costs. The company's copper business saw record EBITDA growth of 73%, while the aluminium business benefitted from improved operational efficiencies.

articles.headline: July sees record EV retail sales driven by two-wheelers
articles.summary: Electric vehicle (EV) retail sales in India reached a record 3.28 lakh units in July, representing a 66% year-on-year growth. The surge was primarily driven by the two-wheeler segment, which saw a 88% increase. Three-wheelers and passenger vehicles also posted gains. Market penetration for EVs reached 3.57% of total vehicle sales, up from 1.32% a year ago.

articles.headline: TVS VMS joins hands with Montra Electric for e-trucks
articles.summary: TVS Vehicle Mobility Solutions has partnered with Montra Electric to deploy electric medium and heavy commercial vehicles. The collaboration will start with a pilot project in Chhattisgarh using Montra's e-trucks for freight operations. The initiative aims to provide total cost of ownership benefits to customers while contributing to India's net-zero carbon goals.

articles.headline: Ola Electric sees sharp recovery in volumes in June quarter
articles.summary: Ola Electric reported a narrowed loss of ₹336 crore for Q1 FY27, compared to ₹450 crore a year ago. Revenue fell 45% due to a sharp sequential recovery in volumes, with 39,192 units delivered. The company's market share in the electric two-wheeler segment rose to 8.4% in June. Operations were supported by a broader regional cluster strategy and expansion in the North and East.

articles.headline: Raw material costs will likely peak in Sept quarter: Satish Pai
articles.summary: Hindalco Industries Managing Director Satish Pai expect raw material costs to peak in the September quarter before declining. He noted that while coal prices have stabilized, caustic soda and oil prices have started to rise. The company is focusing on brownfield expansions and increasing scrap sourcing to 60-70% over the next three years to manage costs.

articles.headline: JK Tyre & Industries Q1 net down 73% at ₹44 cr
articles.summary: JK Tyre and Industries reported a 73% decline in consolidated net profit to ₹44.09 crore for the June quarter. Revenue from operations remained flat at ₹3,946.24 crore. The profit drop was attributed to higher raw material costs and reduced demand in West Asia, though domestic replacement demand showed some resilience.

articles.headline: Hinduja Global Solutions posts ₹66 crore loss in Q1
articles.summary: Hinduja Global Solutions (HGS) reported a consolidated loss of ₹66.26 crore for the first quarter ended June 30. This compares to a profit of ₹11.16 crore in the same period last year. Consolidated revenue from operations remained nearly flat at ₹1,050.36 crore. Performance was impacted by exceptional items and higher operating expenses.

articles.headline: Chaitanya Rathi back in Sula’s leadership rank as Director
articles.summary: Sula Vineyards has appointed Chaitanya Rathi as an Additional Non-Executive Independent Director. Rathi previously served as the company's Chief Operating Officer from 2019 to 2023. His return follows over a decade of leadership experience in various roles within the organization, including key contributions to Sula’s 2022 IPO.

articles.headline: Forex kitty swells by $10.5 b to record $693 b
articles.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves surged by $10.512 billion to reach a record high of $692.866 billion for the week ended July 31. The increase was driven by a $8.75 billion rise in foreign currency assets, which now stand at $564.68 billion. Gold reserves also increased by $1.73 billion, contributing to the overall boost in the country's external buffers.

articles.headline: OMCs begin testing for E20 fuel contamination at pumps from July
articles.summary: Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) have started rigorous testing at 90,000 retail outlets to address concerns of water and chloride contamination in E20 fuel. Union Minister Hardeep Singh Puri stated that 2,000 samples are being collected daily. Only four cases of contamination were found out of 1.07 lakh tests, which the ministry attributed to local storage issues.

articles.headline: RE sector gains momentum with ₹5.25/unit RTC tariff discovery
articles.summary: The renewable energy (RE) sector saw a competitive tariff of ₹5.25 per unit discovered for Round-the-Clock (RTC) RE power in a recent SECI bid. MNRE Secretary S.N. Sahai noted this demonstrates the competitiveness of RE-plus-storage technologies. India's installed RE capacity has crossed 300 GW, moving toward the 500 GW non-fossil fuel target by 2030.

articles.headline: LS clears MSME Bill to speed up payments and ease business
articles.summary: The Lok Sabha passed the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026, aimed at resolving delayed payments. The Bill mandates a 45-day payment cycle for MSME suppliers and simplifies the dispute resolution process. It also encourages the use of the TReDS platform to improve cash flow and reduce financial stress for small businesses.

articles.headline: NLC India Q1 net profit falls 48% to ₹436 crore
articles.summary: NLC India reported a 48% drop in net profit to ₹436 crore for the quarter ended June 30, down from ₹839 crore a year earlier. The decline was attributed to a deferred tax adjustment of ₹425 crore. Total income rose to ₹4,717 crore, while coal production remained steady at 40.85 lakh tonnes during the quarter.

articles.headline: Toyota Hilux review: A duality of ruggedness and modern styling
articles.summary: The 9th generation Toyota Hilux balances its traditional off-road capabilities with improved styling and refinement. Powered by a 2.8-litre four-cylinder turbo diesel engine, it offers significant torque for heavy-duty tasks. While the interior remains functional and somewhat basic, new 17-inch alloys and LED lights enhance its appeal as a lifestyle pickup truck.

articles.headline: Mini Countryman: Big on character in a homogenous SUV segment
articles.summary: The new Mini Countryman retains its distinct character while growing in size. Priced at ₹47.5 lakh, it features a 2.0-litre three-cylinder engine and a circular OLED display with 'Go-kart' mode. Despite being the largest Mini yet, it maintains the brand's 'fun-to-drive' philosophy and offers a premium alternative to traditional compact luxury SUVs.

articles.headline: Reserve Bank rejects demerger proposal of Religare Enterprises
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has rejected the demerger proposal of Religare Enterprises (REL), which sought to transfer its financial services business to a subsidiary, Religare Finvest (RFL). The RBI stated the application had been examined and the request could not be acceded to, though no specific reasons were disclosed for the rejection.

articles.headline: PFRDA eyes NPS AUM of ₹40 lakh cr in four years
articles.summary: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) expects Assets Under Management (AUM) for the National Pension System (NPS) to reach ₹40 lakh crore in the next four years. Chairman S. Bandyopadhyay noted current AUM is around ₹18 lakh crore, with growth driven by increasing subscriptions from the non-government sector and digital onboarding.

articles.headline: ICICI Lombard unveils motor cyber insurance for connected cars
articles.summary: ICICI Lombard has launched India's first motor cyber insurance policy to protect connected car owners against hacking and data theft. The cover addresses risks such as unauthorized vehicle access, software corruption, and financial losses from digital wallet breaches. The product is an optional rider as vehicles become more software-driven and vulnerable to cyber threats.

articles.headline: As aviation demand surges, Safran explores expanding India presence
articles.summary: French aerospace major Safran is considering expanding its footprint in India beyond engine manufacturing. The company sees potential in aircraft interiors, cabin equipment, and maintenance services as Indian airlines place orders for over 2,000 planes. Safran aims to triple its India revenue by 2030 and double its local supplier base.

articles.headline: UPI services to remain free for consumers, says govt
articles.summary: The Union government clarified that Unified Payments Interface (UPI) services will continue to be free for consumers. Responding to social media speculation, the Ministry of Finance stated there is no proposal to levy any charges for UPI transactions. The government continues to provide financial support for the digital payment ecosystem to ensure its growth.

articles.headline: Carborundum Universal Q1 profit rises 23% to ₹88 crore
articles.summary: Carborundum Universal reported a 23% rise in consolidated net profit to ₹88 crore for the quarter ended June 30. Sales grew 17% to ₹1,411 crore, supported by strong performance in the abrasives and electro-minerals segments. The company declared a one-time dividend of ₹68 crore received from a subsidiary during the quarter.

articles.headline: SC judgment won't have big impact on motor third-party portfolio
articles.summary: Shriram General Insurance stated that a recent Supreme Court judgment recognizing the economic value of unpaid domestic work will not significantly impact motor third-party insurance portfolios. Managing Director Anil Aggarwal noted that while claims may see adjustments based on domestic care valuation, the overall impact on the general insurance industry is expected to be limited.

articles.headline: Oil India Q1 profit nearly doubles to ₹4,027 cr
articles.summary: State-run Oil India reported a consolidated net profit of ₹4,027 crore for Q1, up from ₹2,036 crore a year ago. The surge was aided by higher crude oil production and robust profits from its subsidiary Numaligarh Refinery. Crude production reached 0.950 million tonnes, its highest-ever daily rate. The company also reported successful exploratory drilling in Assam and the Andaman Basin.

articles.headline: FSSAI slaps fine on AWL Agri Business for 'substandard' oil
articles.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has imposed a penalty on AWL Agri Business Ltd for manufacturing substandard edible oil. Tests revealed that Vitamin A and Vitamin D levels were significantly lower than prescribed standards. The company is reviewing the order and plans to pursue legal remedies, maintaining that their products meet FSSAI norms.

articles.headline: RBI’s draft lending norms weaken NBFC stocks, drag Sensex, Nifty
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India’s draft proposal to restrict non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) from certain credit facilities triggered a sell-off in NBFC stocks. Bajaj Finance, Bajaj Finserv, and Cholamandalam Investment saw significant drops, dragging the Sensex down 455 points. The draft suggests limiting NBFCs to term loans, effectively curbing flexible lending and over-draft products.

articles.headline: More SEBI orders fail to withstand SAT review in 2025-26
articles.summary: The Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) set aside 47 orders of the SEBI in 2025-26, more than double the 23 appeals it allowed the previous year. While SAT upheld some orders, it modified directions in cases involving insider trading and takeover regulation violations. The trend highlights a need for SEBI to strengthen its reasoning and investigative evidence in adjudication proceedings.

articles.headline: SEBI streamlines inspections of market intermediaries, cuts routine visits
articles.summary: SEBI has revamped its inspection framework for market intermediaries to focus on risk-based oversight. Key changes include reducing the number of routine inspections while increasing targeted, data-driven audits. The regulator also adopted an enhanced inspection framework after discussions with stock exchanges and depositories, aimed at improving the ease of doing business for brokers.

articles.headline: LIC gains 1.7% as brokerages upgrade targets after Q1 beat
articles.summary: LIC shares rose 1.7% after the insurer reported strong Q1 results, including a better-than-expected Value of New Business (VNB) margin. Net profit reached ₹13,490 crore for the quarter. Major brokerages like Motilal Oswal and Jefferies raised their target prices for LIC, citing margin expansion and a shift in product mix toward higher-margin non-participating policies.

articles.headline: NSE moots tighter oversight of authorised persons, stricter eligibility
articles.summary: The National Stock Exchange (NSE) has proposed a stricter regulatory framework for authorised persons (APs). The proposal includes raising the minimum eligibility age to 21, requiring at least two years of market experience, and a minimum net-worth of ₹5 lakh. The move aims to curb market misconduct and strengthen investor protection by ensuring APs are better qualified and supervised.

articles.headline: Ardee Industries IPO subscription hits over 133 times
articles.summary: Ardee Industries' ₹426-crore IPO received a massive response, with the issue being subscribed 133.66 times on its final day. Institutional investors led the demand with a subscription of 197.77 times, while the retail portion was subscribed 45.71 times. The IPO was priced at ₹30-32 per share, and the proceeds will be used for debt repayment and general corporate purposes.

articles.headline: Trump order sets 15% tariff, price floors on polysilicon imports
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump signed a proclamation imposing a 15% tariff and setting price floors on imported polysilicon used in solar products. The move targets imports from China and Southeast Asia to encourage domestic production and protect national security. Solar manufacturers in the US welcomed the measure, though it may raise costs for some renewable energy developers.

articles.headline: Social media accounts of foreign journalists applying for US visa scrutinized
articles.summary: The US State Department is implementing a new policy to vet the social media accounts of foreign journalists applying for visas. The 'online presence vetting' aims to ensure applicants meet security standards and do not pose a threat. The move has raised concerns among media organizations about its potential impact on investigative reporting and press freedom.

articles.headline: India not in favour of BRICS currency: Piyush Goyal
articles.summary: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal stated that India is not currently in favour of a common BRICS currency. He emphasized that any such move requires careful consideration of the diverse economic and financial systems within the group. India remains focused on strengthening its own currency and bilateral trade settlements in rupees with other member nations.

articles.headline: Investments in gold ETFs continue to be net positive
articles.summary: Gold Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) saw net inflows of $1.3 billion globally for the second week in a row. Inflows in Asia and India remained strong, while US-led outflows totaled $900 million as some investors booked profits. Year-to-date, gold ETFs have seen net inflows of $7.8 billion, with Indian investors remaining steadfast buyers as gold prices hover near $4,330 per ounce.

articles.headline: Oilseeds’ acreage up 3% as monsoon revives across India
articles.summary: Kharif oilseed sowing has increased by 3% to 119.92 lakh hectares as monsoon rains improved across major growing states. Groundnut acreage rose 9%, while soyabean and sesamum also saw gains. However, castor area declined by 23%, particularly in Gujarat. Officials remain optimistic that continued rains in August will further boost sowing and improve crop yields.

articles.headline: Groundnut area expands as farmers bet on MSP and rain
articles.summary: Groundnut acreage in India has risen by 9% to 46.82 lakh hectares, driven by better monsoon coverage and attractive Minimum Support Prices (MSP). Sowing increased significantly in Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh. The government's procurement support and timely rains have encouraged farmers to expand cultivation, offsetting minor declines in Gujarat and Karnataka.

articles.headline: Twin lows to help monsoon’s fresh surge in South India
articles.summary: Two new low-pressure areas forming over the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea are expected to trigger a fresh surge in the kharif monsoon. Weather models predict widespread rainfall over Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and parts of South India. This atmospheric activity, linked to a positive Indian Ocean Dipole, is likely to strengthen rains through August and September.

articles.headline: Cultivable land down but area under crops increases, says govt
articles.summary: Total cultivable land in India decreased from 181.28 million hectares in 2014-15 to 179.43 million hectares in 2022-23. However, the gross cropped area increased from 198.28 million to 225.19 million hectares due to better irrigation and double-cropping practices. Horticulture production also reached a record 350 million tonnes, reflecting higher land productivity.

articles.headline: Parag Milk Foods to double cheese production capacity by FY28
articles.summary: Parag Milk Foods Ltd (PMFL) plans to double its cheese production capacity from 60 tonnes to 120 tonnes per day by FY28. The ₹105-crore expansion at its Manchar plant will be funded through internal accruals and debt. The move aims to meet growing demand from the retail and HoReCa segments, further strengthening the company's 'Go Cheese' brand in the Indian market.

articles.headline: Home Ministry alerts corporates on ‘Boss Scam’ malware via WhatsApp
articles.summary: The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) issued an alert regarding 'Boss Scam' malware being spread via WhatsApp. The malware uses social engineering to trick employees, particularly CFOs and accountants, into making unauthorized fund transfers. The ministry advised companies to use multi-factor authentication and block suspicious file types to prevent cyber fraud.

articles.headline: Centre creates 1,500 CDSCO posts for medical devices regulation
articles.summary: In a boost to India's medical device ecosystem, the government announced 1,500 new posts at the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO). The new positions include specialists in ophthalmic devices and internal regulatory systems. The move aims to improve clinical investigation standards and support India's goal of becoming a global hub for medical technology.

articles.headline: AP unveils pedestrian safety policy for child-friendly road infrastructure
articles.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government launched its 'Pedestrian Safety & Universal Accessibility Policy, 2026'. The policy mandates child-friendly and accessible footpaths, tactile paving, and better-lit crossings. It aims to reduce pedestrian fatalities and ensure roads are inclusive for senior citizens and persons with disabilities. The project will initially target 20 high-traffic roads.

articles.headline: HAL starts India's first satellite-guided navigation for choppers
articles.summary: Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL) launched India's first satellite-guided precision navigation system for helicopters in Bengaluru. The system improves safety during low-visibility flights and search-and-rescue operations by providing precise flight path guidance. This indigenous technology reduces noise pollution over cities and marks a major milestone in Indian aviation tech.

articles.headline: JNPA earned more revenue despite lower shipping volumes in FY26
articles.summary: The Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (JNPA) reported higher revenues in FY26 despite a slight drop in container volumes. Revenue reached ₹3,437 crore, driven by improved operational efficiency and higher tariff realizations. JNPA maintained its position as India's second-largest major port, handling significant cargo for the chemical, power, and manufacturing sectors.

articles.headline: India seeks China river data as Tibet dam raises concerns
articles.summary: India is pressing China to resume sharing hydrological data for trans-border rivers as Beijing constructs a large dam on the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet. New Delhi raised concerns about the dam's potential impact on water flows and local environments in downstream Indian states. The two countries are discussing the revival of a data-sharing agreement to manage flood risks.

articles.headline: Akasa Air ramps up operations with three new aircraft
articles.summary: Akasa Air has expanded its fleet with three new Boeing 737 aircraft, bringing its total fleet to 23. The airline plans to add more international routes and increase flight frequency on domestic sectors. CEO Vinay Dube stated that the expansion is part of the airline's long-term growth strategy to capture a larger share of the growing Indian aviation market.

articles.headline: Celebs boost digital endorsement deals to record ₹71,621 crore
articles.summary: The Indian digital advertising market reached ₹71,621 crore, driven by a surge in celebrity endorsement deals. Shah Rukh Khan, Ranveer Singh, and Alia Bhatt led the rankings in brand value and endorsement volume. The trend reflects a shift from traditional TV ads to digital-first social media campaigns, which now account for over 60% of total celebrity brand associations.

articles.headline: Electoral enumeration deadline extended
articles.summary: The enumeration phase of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) for electoral rolls in Karnataka has been extended until August 17. The draft rolls will now be published on August 24, with claims and objections running till September 23. The final rolls are due October 27. This is the second extension granted for the exercise.

articles.headline: Bengaluru city police to be restructured on GBA lines?
articles.summary: Bengaluru City Police is set for restructuring, potentially creating five commissionerates (Central, East, West, North, South) with a Chief Police Commissioner. Each commissionerate would have 2-4 law & order and 1-2 traffic divisions. The move, mirroring the GBA structure, aims to decentralize administration, though concerns exist about dual authority and traffic management.

articles.headline: Namma Metro’s Blue Line achieves over 72% progress
articles.summary: Bengaluru Metro's Blue Line (Phase 2A and 2B), connecting Central Silk Board Junction to Kempegowda International Airport, has achieved 72.5% physical progress. The Union government has released ₹26,447.27 crore for various Namma Metro phases. The 58.19-km corridor comprises 29 stations.

articles.headline: Halt enforcement action against bike taxis: Association
articles.summary: The Namma Bike Taxi Association urged the Karnataka government to halt enforcement against bike taxi riders. They allege transport authorities failed to provide guidelines for legal compliance despite a High Court order. The association demands suspension of actions, clear conversion guidelines, and inclusion of unions in policy framing.

articles.headline: BMTC: Students on NICE Road must pay toll
articles.summary: Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC) clarified that students using BMTC buses on NICE Road must pay the applicable toll fee if alternative routes exist. Free bus pass holders are exempt only when no alternative roads are available, such as routes to Doddaballapura and Kanakapura.

articles.headline: Minister Krishna Byre Gowda in #THTalksBengaluru
articles.summary: Krishna Byre Gowda, Greater Bengaluru Development Minister, will participate in 'THTalksBengaluru' on August 13. Readers can submit questions to him via email. Gowda, a six-time MLA, holds key portfolios for Bengaluru's civic action, with civic polls expected this year.

articles.headline: BDA to launch website for sapling maintenance updates
articles.summary: Following questions about the fate of 1.5 million saplings planted on June 27, the BDA has called a short-term tender to create a website for live maintenance updates. The authority claims 90% of saplings are thriving, with 279 sites successful and 27 distressed. All saplings are geotagged.

articles.headline: Japanese man compensated after 7-year jail battle in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Japanese national Hirotoshi Tanaka received ₹75,000 compensation from the Karnataka government after a 7-year legal battle. The KSHRC ruled he was unnecessarily jailed for 19 days in 2019 following a dispute with an English academy and alleged police misconduct, including bribery demands. Disciplinary action against an officer was initiated.

articles.headline: Govt. departments to get notices for waste clearance
articles.summary: Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda ordered civic bodies to issue notices to government departments failing to clean their premises. Since August 1, the 'Freedom from Waste' campaign has cleared 10,056 tonnes of C&D waste from 453 public sites. 3,022 illegal dumping sites, holding 59,823 tonnes of debris, have been identified.

articles.headline: Man held for murdering wife in Bengaluru
articles.summary: A man from Bihar, Dhiraj Kumar, has been arrested in Bihar for allegedly murdering his wife, Reema Kumari, in Bengaluru. He fled to his native place after the crime. Police reported that frequent quarrels between the couple, who had married 10 months ago, led to the murder.

articles.headline: Tiger, leopard scents aid wildlife monitoring: Study
articles.summary: NCBS researchers developed a non-invasive method using volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in urine and scat to identify age, sex, and reproductive status of tigers and leopards. This tool, supported by National Geographic Society, offers conservationists a way to track these elusive big cats, improving population health and safety monitoring.

articles.headline: Bengaluru varsity inducts student leaders
articles.summary: Kristu Jayanti University in Bengaluru held an investiture ceremony on Friday to induct newly elected student leaders for the academic year 2026-27. Student secretaries for over 60 clubs, associations, and academies were part of the induction.

articles.headline: Astrobase unveils India’s first privately built 800kN rocket engine
articles.summary: Astrobase, a Bengaluru-based space company, unveiled EVEREST, India’s first privately built 800 kN Full-Flow Staged Combustion (FFSC) LOX-Methane rocket engine. This makes India the fourth nation with FFSC technology. The engine is designed for reusable medium-lift launch vehicles, aiming for launch-on-demand capability.

articles.headline: Renukaswamy murder case: 2 accused seek to turn approvers
articles.summary: Two accused in the Renukaswamy murder case, in which Kannada actor Darshan is implicated, have approached a Bengaluru court to turn approvers. Pradosh, Darshan’s confidant, filed an 11-page application, and Vinay (Accused No. 10) also sought pardon. The court reserved its decision until Monday.

articles.headline: FIR filed against Hindu Samiti member for misinformation
articles.summary: Police booked Mohan Gowda of Hindu Janajagruti Samiti for allegedly spreading misinformation on social media about the shifting of comedian Kunal Kamra’s show in Whitefield, Bengaluru. Gowda allegedly filmed a video claiming the Samiti demanded the show be stopped and an inspector promised action, which police denied.

articles.headline: Cong. explores options for Karnataka Cabinet expansion
articles.summary: The Congress leadership in Karnataka is exploring options to balance gender, regional, caste, and community representation in the Cabinet, amid demands from ministerial aspirants and criticism for excluding women legislators. Proposals include dropping a Vokkaliga Minister for M. Krishnappa or replacing Mandya Ministers for regional balance.

articles.headline: HC bars final KPSC scam reports without permission
articles.summary: The Karnataka High Court directed the CID and Vidhana Soudha police not to file final reports on their probes into alleged recruitment scams in the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) without its prior permission. The court also said no coercive action against provisionally selected candidates for veterinary officer posts.

articles.headline: Karnataka unveils special package for handloom sector
articles.summary: Karnataka will allocate a special package for its handloom sector under the forthcoming Textile and Apparel Policy to preserve heritage, strengthen weavers' livelihoods, and position products nationally and globally. Secretary Rohini Sindhuri also launched ‘Our Heritage. Our Threads. Our Future’ social media campaign.

articles.headline: HAL airport pioneers new helicopter approach system
articles.summary: HAL airport in Bengaluru is India's first to operationalize the RNP CAT H helicopter approach procedure, a satellite-guided precision navigation system developed by AAI. This system reduces approach time, enhances safety, efficiency, and accessibility for helicopter operations, and sets a benchmark for other airports.

articles.headline: Cong. MLC wants sanitation worker to open Mysuru Dasara
articles.summary: Congress MLC B.S. Shivanna urged the Karnataka government to have a pourakarmika (municipal sanitation worker) inaugurate the 2026 Mysuru Dasara festival. This suggestion aims to recognize their invaluable contribution to keeping cities clean and healthy, deviating from the traditional inauguration by eminent personalities.

articles.headline: Centre considering law to protect women farmers
articles.summary: The Union government is considering legislation to protect women farmers' rights, inspired by Maharashtra's 2026 Act, said S. Mahendra Dev, Chairman of the Economic Advisory Council to the PM. He emphasized placing women at the center of agrifood systems, shifting to an income-centric approach via crop diversification and better marketing.
